description.promeva:title: Description (English)
description.narrative:
CARE Nederland and CARE Yemen, together with consortium partners, RNW Media and SOS Center for Youth Capabilities Development (SOS), formed a Consortium’, to implement the program titled ‘Women, Peace, and Security (WPS) in Yemen. The overall aim of this program is to improve women’s meaningful influence in relief, recovery and peace processes in Yemen, in Taiz and Eden. The program will contribute to all three sub-objectives of the Dutch WPS grant instrument, including strengthening the protection for women, addressing harmful social norms, and increasing opportunities for women’s meaningful participation in relief, recovery, and peacebuilding, as well as supporting the priorities of the Netherlands Cooperation in Yemen. The program also supports the implementation of sustainable development goals (SDGs) 5 and 16, focusing on gender equality and on peaceful and inclusive societies, respectively. The goals of the NAP are particularly relevant for Yemen’s ongoing, multi-track peace process. To varying degrees, the peace process engages women via Track 1, which involves official diplomatic efforts and formal negotiations; Track 2, which involves consultations with civil society organizations (CSOs). And Track 3, which refers to community-level initiatives for peacebuilding and conflict prevention. The Consortium’s WPS programming aims to strengthen the involvement of women in the different tracks of the peace process (with more emphasis on tracks 2 and 3) and women’s role in relief and recovery. Moreover, it aims to strengthen women’s protection from SGBV and influence social norms that constrain or undermine women’s participation and protection to build a more supportive environment for women’s inclusion in peace and security.
The TOC is built around three sub-objectives and four domains of change. Sub-Objective 1: More equitable social norms and related practices Sub-Objective 2: Enhanced protection for women Sub- Objective 3: More inclusive relief, recovery, and peace processes
Domain of Change 1: Civil society is capable, representative, engaged in collective action Domain of Change 2: Male awareness and support to women’s contributions and leadership Domain of Change 3: Powerholders are more supportive to women Domain of Change 4: Women are empowered to influence relief/recovery/peacebuilding
